name: Dominica
snapshot: The "nature island" of the Caribbean, rebuilt after Hurricane Maria in 2017 with a plan to become the first climate-resilient nation, led by Roosevelt Skerrit since 2004.
culture: Dominica is home to the Kalinago, the last surviving pre-Columbian Caribbean people, with their own territory on the east coast. Its French-based Creole, Kwéyòl, reflects alternating French and British rule. The World Creole Music Festival features bouyon, a local genre. Rainforests, a boiling lake and whale watching anchor tourism.
society: Hurricane Maria in 2017 damaged nearly every building and caused losses of more than twice the island's GDP. Citizenship by investment funds much of the reconstruction. Agriculture, especially bananas, has declined. Skerrit's Dominica Labour Party has won every election since 2000.
situation: Roosevelt Skerrit won a sixth term in a 2022 snap election boycotted by the main opposition party. Sylvanie Burton, the first Kalinago head of state, became president in 2023.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the House of Assembly; the president is elected by parliament and largely ceremonial.
